sections.html:
Cape Girardeau sits on the Mississippi River in Southeast Missouri, along Interstate 55 between St. Louis and Memphis. Population was estimated at 40,977 on July 1, 2025.

The middle owned home is worth $196,300, and only 54.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $876. A university and two large hospitals shape who buys and moves here. Since barely half of homes are owner-occupied, a former rental is a common sight.

The city is mostly in the Cape Girardeau Public Schools district, with a section of Cape Girardeau County in the Jackson R-II district. A small part of the city lies in Scott County, where Scott City R-I covers most of that area. Check your parcel before you tell a buyer which district applies, and note the county too, because the county decides which assessor and recorder you call.

Houses near the Mississippi depend on the floodwall and levee, which the Army Corps of Engineers finished in 1964 and the city now owns and maintains. The city's online maps include a flood zone layer, which is the place to check a parcel near the river before a buyer asks.

The city licenses residential rentals and enforces a checklist of safety and condition standards through Inspection Services at City Hall, 44 N. Lorimier Street, phone 573-339-6327. Standards include working smoke alarms in every bedroom, in the hallway outside bedrooms and on each floor, bedroom egress windows with a clear opening of at least 24 inches high and 30 inches wide, handrails on steps with four or more risers, and guards on landings more than 30 inches high.

If tenants live there, check with the department that the license is current. Investor buyers will ask.

For repair work, inspection requests received after 11:30 a.m. are scheduled for the next day, final inspections need 24 hours notice, and approved plans must be on site. Local historic districts have their own review: the Historic Preservation Commission handles Certificate of Appropriateness applications. Ask the planning division whether your street is in one before you plan exterior changes.

The county assessor, whose office is at 1 Barton Square, Suite 201 in Jackson, values every parcel. Missouri law calls for existing real property to be reassessed every odd-numbered year as of January 1. New improvements get added once construction is done.

Tax rates come from the school, library, fire and other districts, not from the assessor. The assessor's website has a real estate search and parcel map, and the office handles Missouri Property Tax Credit form 948 for qualifying seniors and disabled owners. Call 573-243-2468 or email appraisal@capecounty.us for value questions.

Ask the Cape Girardeau County Collector for your current bill, and ask your closing agent how the year gets divided.

sections.h2: Getting a house ready for a buyer's inspection
sections.html:
Whether the house was ever a rental or not, a buyer's inspector will look at the same safety items the city checks. Walk through before you list. Test the smoke alarms in each bedroom, the hallway outside the bedrooms and on every floor. Make sure bedroom windows open fully, since egress windows need a clear opening at least 24 inches high and 30 inches wide. Look at steps with four or more risers for handrails, and at any landing higher than 30 inches for a guard.

These are inexpensive fixes next to the cost of a failed rental inspection or a buyer who walks away from a repair list. If you pull permits for the work, schedule inspections early in the day, because requests received after 11:30 a.m. roll to the next day and final inspections need 24 hours notice.

A rental in Cape Girardeau has two clocks running: the lease and the city license. Start by asking Inspection Services at 573-339-6327 whether the license is current and whether any inspection items are open. Then tell the tenants about your plans and ask when showings or a buyer's walkthrough can happen. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants will want the license status, the lease terms and the rent figure. A buyer who wants the house empty will ask when you can deliver it.

Because so many homes in the city are rentals, you are not unusual, and an investor buyer will know the local rules. Even so, get the license question answered before you agree on a closing date. Keep copies of the license, any inspection results and the lease in one folder, and hand them to the title company with your mortgage payoff request so the closing office has everything in one place.

Send deeds to the county Recorder of Deeds, #1 Barton Square, Suite 203, Jackson. The phone is 573-243-8123, and weekday hours are 8:00 to 4:30. Documents can be mailed, dropped off or e-recorded.

A standard document costs $24 for page one and $3 for each page after. If it misses the formatting standards, add $25. Pages must be 8.5 by 11 inches, with a three inch margin on the first page left blank for the recorder's stamp. Staff cannot draft documents or give legal advice, so an attorney or title agent prepares the deed.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Cape Girardeau house fast
sections.html:
Owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or ask investors for direct offers. With many renters and a lower price range, houses needing work or carrying tenants can linger, which is why some owners choose a fast as-is sale.

Before choosing, collect four things: rental license status, the county tax bill, the mortgage payoff and the school district for the address. Those items settle most of the questions that come up between a signed contract and closing day.

With a cash buyer there is no bank in the middle, so nothing waits on loan approval or a lender's appraisal. Title work, the tax payoff and the deed recording still happen, and the county offices above are where you get the paperwork. For a rental, ask the buyer what they plan for the tenants, and settle the license question before picking a closing date.

faqs.q: Is Cape Girardeau in one county?
faqs.a: Mostly it is in Cape Girardeau County, but a small part of the city lies in Scott County. Check the parcel's county before calling an assessor or recorder.

faqs.q: Where does a Cape Girardeau deed get filed?
faqs.a: The Cape Girardeau County Recorder of Deeds in Jackson, at #1 Barton Square, Suite 203. A standard deed costs $24 on page one plus $3 per extra page, plus $25 if formatting rules are not met.

faqs.q: How often does the county reassess my house?
faqs.a: State law requires reassessment as of January 1 of every odd-numbered year. The assessor also adds new improvements as construction finishes, so a remodel can change the value in any year.

faqs.q: Does my rental house need a license before I sell it?
faqs.a: The city requires residential rental licensing and inspects against a safety checklist. Call Inspection Services at 573-339-6327 to confirm your unit's status, since buyers who plan to keep tenants will ask.

faqs.q: What flood concerns affect Cape Girardeau homes?
faqs.a: Houses near the Mississippi River depend on the floodwall and levee built in 1964. The city publishes interactive maps with flood zone layers, so check your parcel there.
